title: Join related tables
summary: merge combines tables using shared keys. Check whether each key is unique before deciding how the join should behave.
introduction: merge combines tables using shared keys. Check whether each key is unique before deciding how the join should behave. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: merge combines tables using shared keys. Check whether each key is unique before deciding how the join should behave.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

teams = pd.DataFrame({"team": ["red", "blue"], "room": ["A", "B"]})
joined = df.merge(teams, on="team", validate="many_to_one")
print(joined.loc[joined["name"] == "Ben", "room"].iloc[0])
blocks.title: Join related tables

blocks.text: The output is B. Ben's blue team matches room B in the second table.
